name: add-key-nonallowlisted
why: a single add_key() from a process outside the keyring allowlist is the anchor the rule fires on
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c's add_key(type, desc, payload, plen=7, KEY_SPEC_PROCESS_KEYRING) record. auditd logs a0..a3 (type/desc/payload ptrs, plen); the target keyring is a4 and is not in a0..a3. exit is the decimal key serial, not hex

name: add-key-burst
why: a rapid burst of add_key() from one non-allowlisted pid (the keyring-stuffing primitive); each call independently satisfies the rule
source: recorded: strace of keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c -- three add_key records with decimal key-serial exits and a3=plen(7)

name: keyctl-clear-not-add-key
why: keyctl() reads/updates existing keys and is far more common than add_key; it keeps the keyring-syscall surface, so the syscall==add_key anchor must be load-bearing (the atomic itself issues keyctl(KEYCTL_CLEAR, KEY_SPEC_PROCESS_KEYRING) for cleanup)
source: recorded: strace of keyring_stuffing_behavioral.c cleanup -- keyctl(KEYCTL_CLEAR=7, KEY_SPEC_PROCESS_KEYRING=0xfffffffe)

name: keyctl-join-session-not-add-key
why: keyctl(KEYCTL_JOIN_SESSION_KEYRING) is what a login/PAM path runs to set up a session keyring; same keyring surface, different syscall, so it must not fire. This replaces a prior request_key near-miss: request_key is NOT in detections/audit/atomic.rules and can never reach this pipeline, whereas keyctl is audited
source: synthetic: keyctl(KEYCTL_JOIN_SESSION_KEYRING=1) from a non-allowlisted process; keyctl is audited, request_key is not

name: systemd-allowlisted
why: systemd adds a 'user' key (invocation_id) to the session keyring for every unit it starts with a KeyringMode; the comm allowlist alone must suppress it
source: recorded via source: systemd src/core/exec-invoke.c:3403 add_key("user", "invocation_id", ...) in setup_keyring(); comm 'systemd'

name: gssproxy-allowlisted
why: gssproxy installs Kerberos credentials into the keyring via libkrb5's KEYRING ccache (add_key); the allowlisted GSSAPI identity must be filtered
source: recorded via source: krb5 lib/krb5/ccache/cc_keyring.c:713 add_key(cred key type, ...); libkrb5 is the add_key path for gssproxy/rpc.gssd

name: unrelated-write
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor
